items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: instead of playing a little piece by Mozart this time I’m going to play “Pipeline” by the Chantays.

ctx.x: Yeah well I think I was already starting to play. Yeah, at 15 you know I was starting to play. I joined the Musicians Union I guess that’s what I’m trying to say. Even up in Thunder Bay, Ontario, which at that time it was two towns in Northern Ontario, Fort William, Fort Arthur, me being from Fort William they amalgamated in 1967 and became Thunder Bay. But in Fort William we had a branch of the Local AF of M up there. I can’t remember the number of the Local now, I should be ashamed of myself. But I sure…

in what we call middle school here now, up there it was junior high (grades 7 or 8) I just made a decision, you know instead of playing a little piece by Mozart this time I’m going to play “Pipeline” by the Chantays. [scats] I had learned how to do all that on the piano.

items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: It’s a little Mozarty and if you think about it.

ctx.x: No kidding? You had the [scats] down in your left hand and all that?

Yeah. Pretty easy to play it. It’s a little Mozarty and if you think about it. [scats] But the [scats] I was just playing a piano gliss I guess but man it was close enough. And that may have been where I said well you know you don’t have to write your own material at all, just do this. I kind of brought the house down because it was just so almost rebellious in nature. I don’t know — it represented so many things. And from that point on, and then in high school you know I would do that, especially when The…

I was going to ask if you negotiated the sometimes intense social atmosphere in high school because you had this persona. You weren’t a jock or you weren’t, I don’t know you might have been a straight A student, but you had the music thing. Did that help you?
